A cube of ice is melting uniformly at a rate of $204\,{\text{cm}}^{3}\text{/min},$ where $x$ is the length of its edge. How fast is each edge of the ice block decreasing when the volume of the cube is $216\,{\text{cm}}^{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $V$ be the volume of the ice cube. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-204\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{min}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ when $V=216\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$

  We start with the formula for the volume of the cube:
  

$$
V={x}^{3}
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Before we plug in the known values, we need to find the value of $x$ when $V=216\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={x}^{3} \\ 216 & ={x}^{3} \\ x & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug $x=6$ and $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-204$ into the expression for $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ -204 & =3(6)^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{17}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sides of the cube are decreasing at a rate of $\frac{17}{9}\,\text{cm}/\text{min}$ at the moment when $x=6\,\text{cm}.$
